links.outcome: Time to initial antimicrobial, SPM alert plus navigator vs SIRS-based alert sites
links.effect: Unadjusted 3.33 h at site A vs 3.22 h at sites B-D (p = 0.437); after matching weights, no difference versus contemporaneous SIRS sites. There was a 2.87 h improvement only versus site A historical data.
links.quote: After adjustment using matching weights, there was no difference in time from threshold SPM score to initial antimicrobial between contemporaneous sites.

links.outcome: Time from emergency department arrival to initial antimicrobial delivery
links.effect: Time to antimicrobials: 3.33 h at site A versus 3.22 h at sites B-D (p = 0.437); adjusted improvement versus site A historical was 2.87 h (p < 0.001).
links.quote: Implementation of an electronic sepsis alert system plus navigator using the Epic SPM showed no difference in time to initial antimicrobial delivery between the contemporaneous SPM alert plus sepsis navigator site and the SIRS-based electronic alert sites within the same health care system.

links.effect: No difference between the SPM alert site and SIRS-based alert sites (3.33 h vs 3.22 h, p = 0.437).
links.quote: Implementation of an electronic sepsis alert system plus navigator using the Epic SPM showed no difference in time to initial antimicrobial delivery between the contemporaneous SPM alert plus sepsis navigator site and the SIRS-based electronic alert sites within the same health care system.

screen.practice: Sepsis alert with electronic navigator workflow versus SIRS-based alert
screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of real deployment comparing clinical outcomes of an Epic Sepsis Prediction Model alert plus sepsis navigator against contemporaneous rule-based alerts and historical controls.
